purpose: Canonical example for bug report quality. Use as a guide for evaluating bug reports.

bug.title: PDF download fails on mobile Safari (iOS 17)
bug.description: When a customer attempts to download an invoice PDF on mobile Safari (iOS 17), the download fails with error 500: 'Blob URL not found'. The issue occurs consistently across all iOS 17 devices and affects approximately 30% of our mobile user base.
stepsToReproduce: Login to the customer portal on iOS 17 Safari
Click on any invoice row to select it
Observe error message: 'Error 500: Blob URL not found'
bug.expectedResult: PDF download starts within 3 seconds, file is saved to device Downloads folder.
bug.actualResult: Error 500 modal appears with message 'Blob URL not found'. No download initiated. Console shows: 'Failed to fetch blob://...'
bug.severityJustification: Core feature (invoice download) is completely broken for iOS users. No workaround available. Affects ~30% of mobile user base.
bug.priorityJustification: High business impact – customers cannot access invoices for tax documentation. Legal compliance risk (invoice retention requirement). High visibility (affects all iOS 17 users).
technicalImpact: Customer cannot download invoices on iOS 17
bug.workaround: None available. Desktop browsers (Chrome, Firefox, Safari macOS) work correctly.

reproductionSteps.evidence: 5 numbered steps, specific and sequential, starting from known state (logged in).

expectedVsActual.evidence: Clear separation: expected (download within 3s) vs. actual (Error 500, no download).

environmentInfo.evidence: Complete: browser (Safari 17.2), OS (iOS 17.2), device (iPhone 15 Pro), environment (Staging), app version (2.8.4).

severityJustified.evidence: Severity 'Major' justified with impact (core feature broken, 30% users affected, no workaround).

priorityJustified.evidence: Priority 'P1' justified with business impact (legal compliance, support volume, user visibility).

acPresence.evidence: 3 acceptance criteria for fix verification (download works, error resolved, console clean).

acTestability.evidence: All AC are SMART: Specific (PDF downloads), Measurable (within 3s, 0 errors), Testable.

sizeRisk.evidence: Well-scoped bug fix. Estimated: M (medium) due to iOS-specific blob handling complexity.

verification.gherkin: Given I am on iOS 17 Safari, when I click 'Download PDF', then the download starts within 3 seconds.
verification.measurement: PDF download initiates, file appears in Downloads folder

verification.gherkin: Given the download completes, when I open the PDF, then it contains all required fields (invoice number, date, total, customer number).
verification.measurement: PDF contains all mandatory fields, no corruption

verification.gherkin: Given the fix is deployed, when I check browser console, then there are no blob URL errors.
verification.measurement: Console shows 0 errors related to blob URLs

whyThisIsReferenceQuality: Title answers What (download fails), Where (mobile Safari), When (iOS 17).
Environment section is complete: browser, OS, device, environment, app version.
Reproduction steps are numbered, sequential, and specific (5 steps, anyone can follow).
Expected vs. Actual clearly separated with concrete outcomes and error messages.
Severity and Priority both justified with data (30% users, legal compliance, support volume).
Frequency and first observed date documented for triage.
Attachments listed (screenshot, logs, HAR, video) for faster debugging.
Acceptance criteria for fix verification in Gherkin format (testable by automation).
howToUseThisReference: Use as a template for structuring bug reports: environment → description → steps → expected/actual → severity/priority.
Compare your bug against this reference: Do you have 3+ reproduction steps?
Check if your expected/actual results are as specific as this reference.
Ensure severity and priority are justified with data (impact, frequency, business risk).
Use the acceptance criteria as a template for fix verification.
differencesFromStory: No 'As a user...' format – bugs use descriptive title (What + Where + When).
Focus on reproduction (steps, environment) vs. user value (so that...).
Requires severity/priority justification – stories use business value instead.
Expected vs. Actual critical – stories use acceptance criteria only.
Attachments (screenshots, logs) highly recommended – optional for stories.
